newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - Feb 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - Feb 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- All or part of Banque Misr's and Misr Insurance's stakes in Misr International Bank/MIBANK, which amount to a total of 48.8 percent of the bank, are expected to be offered for sale through international GDRs.

- An increase in the capital of the National Bank ofEgypt's dividend-paying mutual fund was oversubscribed within two weeks. The capital increase in its first growth fund was 60 percent covered, said deputy chairman of al-Ahli Company for Investment Fund Management, Farid Ibrahim.

- Misr Oil and Soap increased its net profits in six months until the end of December by 0.7 million pounds to 15.2 million pounds ($4.5 million) compared to the same period of the previous year. The profit increase was attributed to expenditure rationalisation.

- Net pre-tax profits of Misr Chemical Industries sharply declined in six months to the end of December to 236,000 pounds from 12.932 million in the same period of the previous year. The fall in profits was caused by the closure of the firm's plants for rehabilitation.
- Nasr Dehydrated Agricultural Products 's pre-tax profits shrank in the six months ending on December 31 to 403,000 pounds from 1.577 million because of fierce competition.

- Helwan Portland Cement increased its net after-tax profits in the first half of the financial year, ending on December 31, by 37.5 percent to 75.358 million pounds from 54.797 million. The figures are not yet audited.
- Development and Popular Houses 's pre-tax, unaudited profits declined in six months to the end of December to 4.55 million pounds from 4.59 million in the same period of the previous year.
- Central Egypt Flour Mills 's pre-tax profits rose in six months to the end of December to 24.74 million pounds from 21.25 million in the same period a year earlier.
- Egyptian Starch and Glucose 's profits fell in six months ending on December 31 to 17.693 million pounds from 18.711 million in the same period of the previous year.
- A public offer in Suez Steel will end today after it was oversubscribed within the first three days. The offer started on February 11.

- Egyptian Financial and Industrial increased its after tax profits in the first six months of the financial 96/97 to 24.1 million pounds from 15.5 million in the same period of the previous financial year.
- A public offer in the new firm Egypt Cement (Qena) will end on Tuesday, after it has already been oversubscribed.
